decision: Merge on code is safe (one-to-one, no unmatched rows)

issue: Both files repeat 7 background columns (program, department, semester, age, sex, marital status, SES) that already sit in Member A's file; checked that every value is identical
decision: Dropped the repeated columns; kept code only as the link. Member C merges on code

issue: Duplicates ignoring code (all columns incl. background): TMD file 1, Beck file 19. Duplicates on the answers alone: TMD 94, Beck 555
decision: Kept all. 455 students answered 0 on every Beck item, so many identical rows are expected and genuine; removing them would delete healthy students and change the class balance

issue: Missing cells in the two raw files: 0
Item values outside the allowed range: TMD items allowed 0-4 (found 0-4); Beck items allowed 0-3 (found 0-3)
Supplied TMD total does not equal the sum of its 22 items for 1 student (code 164: supplied 3, items add up to 64, supplied level 'Absence')
decision: Recomputed tmd_total from the items for everyone. The one wrong supplied total looks like a typing error

issue: Supplied Beck total vs sum of 21 items: 0 mismatches
decision: Recomputed bdi_total from the items anyway (identical); maximum observed total is 48 of a possible 63

issue: Checked the supplied level labels against the dictionary bands (TMD: 0-29 Absence, 30-38 Low, 39-48 Medium, 49-88 High; Beck: 0-10, 11-16, 17-20, 21-30, 31-40, over 40). Mismatches: TMD 1, Beck 0
decision: Rebuilt both level columns from the recomputed totals. Beck 'Extreme' exists in the data (1 student, total 48) and its band is in the dictionary ('over 40')

issue: The dictionary sheet and the questionnaire are both titled 'BDI-2', but the item wording (work difficulty, weight loss in pounds, worry about physical problems, interest in sex, body image) is the ORIGINAL 21-item Beck Depression Inventory, whose standard bands are exactly the ones in the dictionary (0-10 normal ... over 40 extreme)
decision: Report it as the Beck Depression Inventory (original form, bands as in the dictionary). The BDI-II bands (mild 14-19) do NOT apply, so a cut-off of 11 means 'mild mood disturbance or worse' and 17 means 'borderline clinical or worse'. Confirm with the supervisor

issue: Dictionary name for Beck item N is 'Feelings of Worthlessness', but the questionnaire statement for N is about body image ('I am worried that I am looking old or unattractive...')
decision: Keep the column; describe it as body-image concern in the report. It is only part of the total, never a model input

issue: The dictionary sheet for the phone-dependence test is named 'TMDbrief', but it lists the full 22-item Test of Mobile Dependence (Q1-Q22, total 0-88)
decision: Report it as the 22-item Test of Mobile Dependence (TMD), not the brief version

issue: Students who gave the SAME answer to all 22 TMD questions: 12; students with all-zero Beck answers: 455 (37%)
decision: Kept: all-zero Beck answers are plausible for students who feel well and the TMD pattern is rare. Mention the Beck 'floor effect' (many zeros) in the report

issue: Box-plot fences: TMD total -11 to 82 (3 outside); Beck total -12 to 20 (65 above, all above because most students score near 0)
decision: Kept all: both scores are bounded questionnaire totals (0-88, 0-63) and the high Beck scores are the students we most want to detect. No values removed or capped

issue: depressed_flag = Beck total >= 11: 218 of 1220 students (17.9%); dependence_flag = TMD total >= 39: 549 of 1220 (45.0%)
decision: Both targets stored as 0/1. Totals are kept so the team can change a cut-off without re-cleaning

issue: Sensitivity columns: depressed_flag_excl_item_i (Beck total without item I, suicidal ideation, same cut-off; 10 students change group) and depressed_flag_ge17 (106 students, 8.7%, 'borderline clinical or worse')
decision: Not used unless the team decides; they answer the open questions about item I and the cut-off. Never use any Beck column as a model input

issue: All TMD questions are 0-4 ordered numbers, all Beck questions are 0-3 ordered numbers; both level columns are ordered text labels
decision: No scaling or encoding done here on purpose: scaling must be fitted on the training part only (Member C). Level labels are for charts and the report, not model inputs, because they are made from the totals
